##  Data Preparation

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE,message=FALSE}
#Reading in csv file and assigning to data frame object named "text_wide" 
text_wide <- read.csv("TextMessages.csv")
class(text_wide$Group)
text_wide$Group <-factor(text_wide$Group,levels=c(1,2))

#In case we need long format data-
text_long <- pivot_longer(
  text_wide, 
  cols= c("Baseline","Six_months"),
  names_to = "Timepoint",
  values_to = "Text_count"
  )
class(text_long$Timepoint)
text_long$Timepoint<-factor(text_long$Timepoint)

#Moving participant number to the front
text_wide <- text_wide |> relocate("Participant")
text_long <- text_long |> relocate("Participant")

```

## Summary Statistics of Text Messages by Group and Time

```{r, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE,message=FALSE,results='asis'}
#We are first grouping the data by the group number and time-point, then
#computing the summary statistics that we want such as the mean, median, SD,
#range, etc., using dplyr from tidyverse.

sum_stat<- text_long |> 
  group_by(Group,Timepoint) |> 
  summarise(
  N=n(),
  Mean=mean(Text_count),
  SD=sd(Text_count),
  Median=median(Text_count),
  Min=min(Text_count),
  Max=max(Text_count),
  IQR=IQR(Text_count),
  .groups = "drop_last"
)

#To output a clean table of the summary statistics, we are using the kable
#function.

kable(sum_stat,
  caption="Summary Statistics of Text Messages by Group and Time-point",
  digits=2,
  align=c("c","l","c","c","c","c","c","c","c")
)

#At baseline, the two groups had relatively similar mean numbers of text messages. Group 1 had a mean of 64.84 (SD = 10.68), while Group 2 had a slightly higher mean of 65.60 (SD = 10.84). The similar means and standard deviations suggest that the groups had comparable text messaging patterns at the start of the study.

#At six months, both groups experienced a decrease in the mean number of text messages. However, the magnitude of the decrease differed between groups. Group 1 had a mean of 52.96 (SD = 16.33), representing an average decrease of 11.88 messages from baseline. Group 2 had a smaller decrease, with a mean of 61.84 (SD = 9.41), representing a reduction of 3.76 messages.

#When comparing means to medians, most of the subgroups have similar values hinting at symmetrical distributions. We only see a major difference in the six month time-point for group 1 where the median was higher than the mean, suggesting a left skew to the distribution. There were also differences in the variability of text messaging patterns at six months. Group 1 demonstrated greater variability (SD = 16.33) compared to baseline, suggesting that participants' messaging behaviors became more dispersed. This is also reflected in the wider range of values (9–78). In contrast, Group 2 demonstrated less variability at six months (SD = 9.41), with a narrower range (46–79), suggesting more consistent messaging patterns among participants.

```
